sources.name: Chrome DevTools · a11y-debugging
sources.label: Proposed adaptation
sources.purpose: Debug a rendered page using Lighthouse findings, browser issues, the accessibility tree, keyboard input and measurements.
sources.contribution: A useful operational checklist for connecting a failing rendered element with semantic, focus and visual evidence. Inspect specific failing nodes and browser issues before choosing a repair.
sources.decision: Keep only the useful gaps in the existing web reference: preserve the state being audited and recognize unresolved contrast measurements. Rendered-node inspection, computed names, hit regions and execution ownership are already covered locally.
cautions: Its navigation-first audit reloads the page. Preserve the failing dialog, authenticated session or unsaved state when that is the target; Addy explicitly addresses this choice.

The supplied contrast snippet is explicitly approximate. Claude also exercised it in the live T3 browser: #777 text on a white body returned 4.69:1 because the transparent element background was parsed as black; the displayed pair is 4.478:1 and fails normal-text AA. Unresolved backgrounds, alpha or modern color syntax cannot establish a passing measurement.
Its 48 px target recommendation is not the WCAG AA minimum. Bounding-box size alone does not establish the effective hit region, overlap or criterion exceptions.
The orphan-input snippet checks attribute presence, not the computed accessible name. A present aria-labelledby value can still point to missing or empty content.
sources.license: Apache-2.0 (repository license header checked; no source text or snippets incorporated).

inspectedFiles.scope: Full read; contrast snippet exercised with a controlled computed-style stub.

sources.name: Mindrally · accessibility-a11y
sources.label: Covered · no addition
sources.purpose: A general checklist for semantics, ARIA, keyboard support, contrast, forms, media and user preferences.
sources.contribution: Readable introductory coverage and a reminder to include people with disabilities in relevant usability testing.
sources.decision: Do not add a second general accessibility skill. The inspected checklist adds little to the current flow-based contract.
cautions: It presents 44 by 44 pixels as a general minimum without distinguishing AA, AAA and criterion exceptions.
Its general instruction to add keyboard handlers alongside click handlers needs a native-control exception; otherwise a repair can duplicate an action.
BEM, mobile-first CSS and other implementation preferences should not become accessibility acceptance criteria.

sources.name: Alireza Rezvani · a11y-audit
sources.label: Do not adopt as supplied
sources.purpose: Scan frontend source files, calculate color-pair contrast, prioritize repairs and produce an audit report.
sources.contribution: The supported positional contrast command correctly rejects #777777 on white for AA normal text. This working calculation does not establish that the scanner, documented CLI or CI examples form a reliable audit workflow.
sources.decision: Do not install this package or import its scanner into our completion checks. Its documented contract and implemented checks need correction first; the current skill already owns evidence-based findings and manual coverage.
cautions: The documented --format table, --report --output and --fg/--bg commands fail with exit code 2. The scanner actually accepts text/json formats; the contrast checker accepts positional colors.

Two isolated barriers pass the scanner: an unlabelled input with an id, and a click-only div with role=button. It also reports a wrapped, labelled input as critical and role=status without explicit aria-live as serious.
Its WCAG 2.2 reference calls Focus Appearance 2.4.11 AA. The published criterion is 2.4.13 AAA; 2.4.11 AA concerns focus not being entirely obscured.

The CI JSON reader expects violations and wcag, but the scanner emits findings and wcag_criterion. That reader misses six critical findings in the retained sample. The preceding scanner step can still fail the complete GitHub Actions job; the isolated reader result does not prove the whole workflow always passes. Static regex checks also cannot substantiate the promise of finding every A/AA violation.

sources.name: Filip Aladic · better-web-ui / a11y
sources.label: Reference only
sources.purpose: Audit and repair UI accessibility within a broader design system, with component and color-vision references.
sources.contribution: Its component reference explains focus after add/remove actions, appropriate hiding techniques and third-party component verification. The color-vision reference usefully tests complete charts and semantic states, beyond palette swatches.
sources.decision: Keep it as a source of test scenarios. Our current guidance already covers these principles; do not import the full design workflow or add another skill.
cautions: The entrypoint asks for every interactive element to be a Tab stop and for removing tabindex=-1 from focusable elements. Applied to a roving composite, this conflicts with its keyboard model. The linked component reference is more nuanced than the entrypoint.
The required frontend-design dependency can start setup and require brand/audience context before a narrow accessibility repair. That is unnecessary scope for our specialist.

The repository uses a custom license with redistribution conditions, not standard MIT; NOTICE.md records additional lineage and frontend-design declares Apache-2.0. Do not treat the whole package as one uncomplicated MIT donor.
sources.license: Custom repository license; Apache-2.0 declaration in frontend-design; additional attribution chain in NOTICE.md. No material incorporated.

inspectedFiles.scope: Context protocol and dependency sections inspected (lines 1-80); broader design guidance not fully audited.

sources.name: Addy Osmani · web-quality-skills / accessibility
sources.label: Proposed adaptation
sources.purpose: Audit and improve web accessibility against WCAG 2.2, combining live findings, manual interaction and linked patterns.
sources.contribution: This is version 2.0 of the web-quality-skills source family already recorded through GSD version 1.0. Its useful delta includes choosing an audit that preserves the target state. Node-to-component tracing and many updated WCAG checks are already covered locally; consistency across pages is a coherent remaining addition.
sources.decision: Use direct upstream for future updates to the mirrored accessibility entrypoint and reference, while preserving the GSD baseline and its separate audit workflow. Narrow any content adaptation to the existing web reference. Keep addyosmani/agent-skills as a distinct donor; do not count the GSD copy and this source as independent endorsements.
cautions: Its contrast table still uses 18 px regular / 14 px bold for large text. WCAG uses 18 pt / 14 pt; our existing reference already has the correct units.

The linked modal example has a static focusable list and lacks complete return-focus handling. The form example calls focus on a field and then on the summary. Neither should become a universal implementation recipe.

A Lighthouse score is not conformance; the source itself says this. Keep manual keyboard and required assistive-technology evidence, and select available host tools rather than imposing its example stack.

proposals.title: Preserve the state being audited
proposals.text: A reload can erase a dialog, error or unsaved state. Choose a supported check that preserves or reconstructs the intended state, and confirm that state is still present when the check runs. Keep tool-specific audit mode names in the local verification recipe.
proposals.reason: Tracing a defect to its responsible component and rerunning it are already in the skill. The new detail should prevent an audit from silently checking a different state.

proposals.title: Resolve the displayed contrast pair
proposals.text: An element without its own opaque background can report a transparent computed background. Account for the displayed background, compositing, alpha and supported color syntax. A snippet that cannot resolve the pair yields an inconclusive measurement, not a pass.
proposals.reason: Computed names, effective hit regions and occlusion are already covered. Keep this addition specific to the demonstrated contrast failure.

proposals.title: Check consistency across pages
proposals.text: When a flow spans a set of pages, check the relative order of repeated navigation and applicable help mechanisms, and consistent identification of the same function, under WCAG 3.2.3, 3.2.4 and 3.2.6. Respect their scope and user-initiated changes. Consistent Help does not require adding help or showing it on every page.
proposals.reason: This checks a coherent part of the user flow. Adding only the criterion named by one donor would leave the purpose of the change unclear; the reference remains selective rather than a complete WCAG checklist.

validation.reportValidator:
import hashlib
import json
import re
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

root = Path.cwd()
directory = root / 'reports/skill-atlas'
report = json.loads((directory / 'accessibility-source-review.json').read_text())
assert len(report['sources']) == 6
assert len({s['id'] for s in report['sources']}) == 6
assert [s['id'] for s in report['sources'] if s['status'] == 'already-incorporated'] == ['ecc']
assert {s['id'] for s in report['sources'] if s['status'] == 'proposed-adaptation'} == {'devtools', 'web-quality'}
for source in report['sources']:
    assert re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{40}', source['commit'])
    for file in source['inspectedFiles']:
        path = root / '.tmp/accessibility-source-review/upstream' / source['id'] / file['path']
        assert hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == file['sha256'], path
for file in report['localEvidence']:
    assert hashlib.sha256((root / file['path']).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == file['sha256'], file['path']
assert report['sources'][0]['commit'] in (root / 'accessibility/origin.txt').read_text()
assert report['sources'][0]['inspectedFiles'][0]['sha256'] == 'e00991a3f4d47fcf1529dd74a080afcf46137dc5061e70dc6e3da7b27f2ae3f3'

probes = {p['id']: p for p in report['probes']}
assert len(probes) == 10
for name in ['unlabelled-input-with-id', 'mouse-only-role-button']:
    assert probes[name]['exitCode'] == 0
    assert json.loads(probes[name]['stdout'])['findings'] == []
for name, rule in [('labelled-input-without-id', 'form-input-no-label'), ('implicit-live-status', 'aria-live-missing'), ('missing-image-alt', 'img-alt-missing')]:
    assert probes[name]['exitCode'] == 1
    assert [f['rule_id'] for f in json.loads(probes[name]['stdout'])['findings']] == [rule]
for name in ['documented-table-format', 'documented-report-flags', 'documented-contrast-flags']:
    assert probes[name]['exitCode'] == 2
    assert 'error:' in probes[name]['stderr']
assert probes['supported-contrast-pair']['exitCode'] == 1
assert json.loads(probes['supported-contrast-pair']['stdout'])['results'][0]['pass'] is False
assert json.loads(probes['devtools-transparent-background']['stdout'])['contrastRatio'] == '21.00'

class Page(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.ids = []
        self.links = []
        self.inline_code = []
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        attrs = dict(attrs)
        if 'id' in attrs:
            self.ids.append(attrs['id'])
        if tag in ('a', 'link') and 'href' in attrs:
            self.links.append(attrs['href'])
        if tag == 'style' or 'style' in attrs or (tag == 'script' and 'src' not in attrs):
            self.inline_code.append(tag)

html = (directory / 'accessibility-source-review.html').read_text()
page = Page()
page.feed(html)
assert '<html lang="en">' in html
assert len(page.ids) == len(set(page.ids))
assert not page.inline_code
assert all('source-' + source['id'] in page.ids for source in report['sources'])
for source in report['sources']:
    assert source['label'] in html
for href in page.links:
    parts = urlsplit(href)
    if parts.scheme:
        assert parts.scheme == 'https'
        continue
    target = directory / unquote(parts.path) if parts.path else directory / 'accessibility-source-review.html'
    assert target.is_file(), href
    if parts.fragment:
        linked = Page()
        linked.feed(target.read_text())
        assert unquote(parts.fragment) in linked.ids, href
css_hash = hashlib.sha256((directory / 'styles.css').read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]
assert f'styles.css?v={css_hash}' in html
assert 'href="accessibility-source-review.html"' in (directory / 'index.html').read_text()
print('PASS: 6 pinned sources, inspected-file hashes, unchanged local skill hashes, 10 probe interpretations, incorporation states, report links, fragments and stylesheet hash.')
